test_cases.title: Telem App Scheduled at 2 Hz on TDM
test_cases.setup: Build POSIX target with TDM scheduler configuration loaded for telem_app.
procedure: Load the static TDM schedule table used to register telem_app.
Read the configured period for the telem_app slot.
Compute the resulting execution frequency from the period.
Compare the computed frequency to 2 Hz.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Static TDM schedule registers telem_app with a 500 ms period, yielding exactly 2 Hz execution frequency.

test_cases.title: Subscribes to All Required Bus Sources
test_cases.setup: Instantiate telem_app with a mocked software bus that records subscription calls and stubbed telem_lib + stubbed lora_lib for full DI completeness.
procedure: Initialize telem_app against the mock bus.
Capture the set of message IDs that telem_app subscribed to during init.
Compare captured subscriptions against the expected set: GPS, baro, navigation, flight phase, sensor health.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: telem_app registers subscriptions for GPS, baro, navigation, flight phase, and sensor health messages; no required source is missing.

test_cases.title: Delegates Packet Composition to telem_lib
test_cases.setup: Wire telem_app to a mock telem_lib that records compose calls and returns a stub packet, mocked software bus for sensor messages and stubbed lora_lib for the transmit boundary.
procedure: Publish representative GPS, baro, nav, flight phase, and health messages onto the mock bus.
Trigger one telem_app execute cycle.
Assert the mock telem_lib compose API was invoked exactly once.
Assert the inputs passed to compose match the most recent values seen on the bus.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: telem_lib compose API is invoked once per cycle with the latest subscribed bus values; telem_app contains no in-line packet assembly logic.

test_cases.title: Latest Sensor Health Bitmap Embedded in Packet
test_cases.setup: Wire telem_app to a mock bus and a mock telem_lib that captures the composed packet bytes, and a stubbed lora_lib whose transmit calls are captured.
procedure: Publish a sensor health bitmap with a known non-zero pattern on the bus.
Trigger one telem_app execute cycle and capture the packet handed to lora_lib.
Publish a different sensor health bitmap on the bus.
Trigger another execute cycle and capture the second packet.
Decode the health bitmap field of each packet and compare to the value published immediately before that cycle.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Each transmitted packet contains the most recently published sensor health bitmap exactly; no stale or default bitmap is emitted.

test_cases.title: Composed Packet Handed to lora_lib
test_cases.setup: Wire telem_app to a mock lora_lib that records every transmit invocation and its payload, mocked software bus seeded with the relevant input messages and stubbed telem_lib whose compose return values are scripted.
procedure: Populate the bus with valid telemetry source messages.
Trigger one telem_app execute cycle.
Capture the buffer and length passed to the mock lora_lib transmit API.
Compare the buffer to the packet returned by the telem_lib compose mock.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: On each cycle the lora_lib transmit API is invoked exactly once with the packet bytes produced by telem_lib compose.

test_cases.title: Continuous Coverage From Power-On
test_cases.setup: Pico 2 flashed with FT1 image; LoRa ground station configured to log received frames with timestamps; bench power supply for the rocket avionics.
procedure: Start the ground station receiver and begin logging received frames with arrival timestamps.
Apply external power to the avionics and start a stopwatch at the moment power is applied.
Allow the system to run on the bench for at least 10 minutes without intervention.
Remove external power and stop the ground station log.
From the ground station log, compute inter-frame intervals and the offset of the first received frame from power-on.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Ground station log shows the first telemetry frame within 5 seconds of power-on and a continuous stream until power removal with no gap exceeding 2 seconds.

expected_artifacts.name: ground_station_rx_log.csv
expected_artifacts.description: CSV of received telemetry frames with arrival timestamps for the full power-on window.

expected_artifacts.name: bench_run_video.mp4
expected_artifacts.description: Video of the bench run showing power application and the running ground station receiver.

test_cases.title: Continues Cycling After Transmit Failure
test_cases.setup: Wire telem_app to a mock lora_lib whose transmit API can be programmed to return failure on selected cycles, mocked software bus and stubbed telem_lib (the cycle path traverses both).
procedure: Configure the mock lora_lib to return a failure status on the next transmit call.
Trigger one telem_app execute cycle and observe the failure being returned.
Trigger five additional execute cycles back-to-back at the scheduled cadence.
Record the lora_lib transmit invocation count and the cycle index of each invocation.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: telem_app invokes lora_lib transmit on every subsequent cycle after a failure with no skipped cycles, no backoff delay, and no halt of execution.

test_cases.title: Publishes Radio Health Reflecting Last Transmit
test_cases.setup: Wire telem_app to a mock bus that captures published messages and a controllable mock lora_lib, and stubbed telem_lib (compose is invoked en route to lora_lib transmit).
procedure: Configure mock lora_lib transmit to return success and trigger one execute cycle.
Capture the radio health message published by telem_app and verify it indicates success.
Configure mock lora_lib transmit to return failure and trigger another execute cycle.
Capture the new radio health message and verify it indicates failure.
Configure mock lora_lib transmit to return success again, run one more cycle, and verify the published health flips back to success.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The radio health status published each cycle matches the success or failure outcome of that cycle's transmit call across at least one success-failure-success transition.

test_cases.title: POSIX and Pico2 Builds Produce Identical Telemetry
test_cases.setup: Build telem_app for POSIX and Pico2 targets from the same commit. Capture a reference recording of bus messages spanning a representative flight profile.
procedure: Replay the captured bus message recording into the POSIX telem_app build and capture every published telemetry packet to a file.
Replay the same recording into the Pico2 telem_app build (or its host-instrumented harness) and capture every published telemetry packet to a file.
Byte-compare the two output files cycle-by-cycle.
Report any differing cycles and their byte offsets.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: POSIX and Pico2 telemetry outputs are byte-identical across all replayed cycles for the same input recording.

test_cases.title: Post-Landing Recovery Beacon Continues Indefinitely
test_cases.setup: Pico 2 avionics on the bench with LoRa antenna and external power; ground station configured for FT1 frame logging; bus inputs configured (or stubbed) so the flight phase reports LANDED.
procedure: Apply external power and start the ground station log.
Drive the flight phase input through ASCENT, DESCENT, and into LANDED, and confirm the LANDED phase is reported on the bus.
Continue running on bench power for at least 30 minutes after the LANDED transition.
Stop the ground station log and remove external power.
Compute the inter-frame interval distribution from the LANDED transition until power removal.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Ground station log shows continuous telemetry frames for at least 30 minutes after LANDED with no gap greater than 2 seconds, and transmission ceases only when external power is removed.

expected_artifacts.name: post_landing_rx_log.csv
expected_artifacts.description: CSV of received frames with timestamps spanning the LANDED phase to power removal.

expected_artifacts.name: post_landing_run_photo.jpg
expected_artifacts.description: Photo of the bench setup at the end of the post-landing run prior to power removal.

test_cases.title: Deterministic Telemetry for Identical Inputs
test_cases.setup: POSIX build of telem_app driven by a deterministic mock bus that replays a fixed sequence of inputs.
procedure: Run telem_app for N cycles using a fixed input sequence and capture every published telemetry packet to file A.
Reset the process, replay the identical input sequence for the same N cycles, and capture published packets to file B.
Byte-compare files A and B cycle-by-cycle.
Repeat the run a third time and compare against file A to rule out two-sample coincidence.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All three runs produce byte-identical published telemetry files for identical input sequences with no diff at any cycle.

test_cases.title: Compose Uses Latest Value Per Source
test_cases.setup: Wire telem_app to a mock bus that allows multiple updates per source between cycles and a mock telem_lib capturing inputs, and a stubbed lora_lib for the transmit boundary.
procedure: Publish two successive GPS messages on the bus before any execute cycle.
Publish two successive baro messages similarly.
Trigger one telem_app execute cycle.
Inspect the inputs the mock telem_lib received and compare each field to the second (latest) published value for that source.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: telem_lib compose receives the most recent value for each subscribed source; no earlier message is forwarded when a newer one is available.

test_cases.title: Radio Health Published Every Cycle
test_cases.setup: Wire telem_app to a mock bus that counts radio health publications per cycle and a mock lora_lib returning a steady-state status, and a stubbed telem_lib (radio health publish path follows compose-then-transmit).
procedure: Run telem_app for 10 consecutive execute cycles with mock lora_lib returning success.
Count the number of radio health messages published by telem_app over the run.
Repeat with mock lora_lib returning failure for all 10 cycles and count again.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Exactly one radio health status is published per execute cycle in both scenarios, totaling 10 publications per 10 cycles, with status matching the configured outcome.
